I cannot recommend this game in 2026. I would classify this game as a Zelda-like. However, currently there are so many better Zelda-likes that Hob is not worth your time. I would highly recommend something else like Death's Door. There are no bosses, the enemies are pretty repetitive and very dumb, so the combat is not good. It is strange the combat is so bland from the team that made Torchlight. The overall world is pretty interesting because it is built like a giant puzzle box. You will push buttons and pull levers to move the world around. This is cool spectacle but often the button or lever you pull will have an incongruent impact on the world. A tiny button will move mountains, but you can put forth enormous effort to get to a different switch only for it to have a tiny piece. The art and graphics hold up and I like the aesthetic. The plot is told without spoken dialogue and ends with an interesting twist, but since there is little plotting or exposition before the end the overall result is tepid.

I stumbled across Hob while scrolling through Steam and thought, “Alright, this looks interesting.” Picked it up on sale, booted it up… and honestly? At first I was confused. Then it crashed due to outdated graphics drivers. I almost wrote it off.

I’m glad I didn’t.

After fixing the driver issue and giving it another real shot, wow. I was hooked.

The exploration is incredibly satisfying. You press a button, activate a mechanism, and suddenly the world shifts. Entire sections rise, rotate, unfold. The map updates. New paths reveal themselves. You start realizing the world itself is a giant interconnected machine, and every action reshapes it. That feeling of “Wait… what just happened?” quickly turns into “There’s more to explore.”

The underground areas (caves, ruins, whatever you want to call them) are consistently engaging. They challenge you just enough to make you think, but rarely feel unfair. There were multiple moments where I ran back and forth trying to figure something out, only to look up and realize the solution was right there the whole time. That kind of design is satisfying rather than frustrating.

Combat was another pleasant surprise. I set it to easy just to chill, but even then it felt deliberate and tool-driven rather than button-mashy. There’s weight to it. You’re combining abilities and positioning rather than just smashing through enemies. I could absolutely see replaying on a higher difficulty.

The atmosphere deserves special mention. The ambient mechanical sounds, the grinding, shifting, rebuilding of the world, are deeply immersive. There’s something very Dark City-like about watching the environment transform around you. It feels mysterious and slightly alien in the best way.

Overall, Hob is a fantastic experience if you enjoy:
- Exploration-first design
- Environmental puzzles
- A world that evolves as you interact with it
- Light but thoughtful combat
- Strong ambient atmosphere

Don’t let a rough first impression stop you. Once it clicks, it really clicks.

Highly recommended.

Hob is a cute and very relaxed puzzle adventure with a hint of a metroidvania.

I love the believable world. It's just enough alive to not make you feel lonely, but it is not overcrowded either - after all, it IS a wilderness (full of cute animals, only some of which are trying to kill you).

Hob is also very much an adventure - and you'll have to do some heavy lifting. At least I did when I was looking for ways to get places, especially in the late game. However, never once did I have to consult a guide - the puzzle/adventure difficulty is in the sweet spot for me.

There was  a lot of backtracking and running around the map involved, but because the world of Hob feels so nice to be in, I really did not mind (and I don't usually consider myself patient). I also managed to get an overwhelming majority of collectibles by myself, without any guides.

One thing I'd like added is better tracking of separate areas - put them on the map and maybe include the info about their "completion" (whether you found all the collectibles in there) from the get-go.

Hob is a good adventure game that unfortunately struggles to pass into a great adventure game. Visuals are amazing, designs are great, though there are a lot of issues with the gameplay unfortunately. Enemies often have too little time to attack or do way to much damage at the start. It is an issue I have with like hard modes in most where it just makes the intro hard but the actual rest of the game when you get some health is insanely easy. Exploration is fun but it is a bit hard to distinguish what is actually somewhere to go or not sometimes. Jumps that seem doable or an area gated off that looks like everywhere you can already go. Not to mention falling too far just instantly kills you. Aiming can be a pain as well but that's probably more on my depth perception. Combat is take it or leave it, works for what it is but I feel like they want it to be bigger than what it was. Combo moves also felt really inconsistent so I usually just used basic attacks and a charge attack. I think the biggest jank issue I had was the grapple. It sometimes didn't seem to come out, sometimes stopped when I was using it, and jumping off one can feel odd. It sort of sums of my opinion of the whole game, it's fun when working well but when it doesn't it's frustrating. I'd recommend it on a sale, enjoyed my time well enough even if it wasn't ground breaking.

[h1]Einstieg[/h1]
„Hob“ ist ein atmosphärisches Action-Adventure von Runic Games, den Leuten hinter Torchlight. Statt Textboxen oder Dialogen setzt das Spiel komplett auf visuelles Storytelling. Erschienen ist es 2017 und fällt sofort durch seinen ruhigen, fast meditativen Vibe auf. Kein Gelaber, keine Marker-Flut - nur man selbst, die Welt und viele Fragezeichen.

[h1]Handlung / Story[/h1]
Die Story wird nicht erklärt, sondern erlebt. Man landet in einer fremden Welt, deren Maschinen scheinbar kaputt oder vergessen sind. Nach und nach erschließt sich, dass diese Welt einmal im Gleichgewicht war - und nun langsam verfällt. Ich fand es ziemlich stark, wie man Zusammenhänge selbst zusammensetzen muss, statt alles serviert zu bekommen. Man fühlt sich oft klein, aber auch verantwortlich.

[h1]Gameplay[/h1]
Gameplay-technisch ist „Hob“ ein Mix aus Erkundung, Rätseln und leichtem Combat. Der Fokus liegt klar auf Exploration: neue Wege freischalten, Mechaniken aktivieren, Abkürzungen schaffen. Besonders cool ist, wie sich die Welt sichtbar verändert, wenn man Maschinen reaktiviert. Kämpfe sind eher Mittel zum Zweck und nicht der Kern des Spiels.

[h1]Steuerung[/h1]
Die Steuerung ist insgesamt sauber und intuitiv. Movement fühlt sich flüssig an, gerade beim Klettern und Springen. In hektischeren Kämpfen kam es bei mir aber gelegentlich zu kleinen Ungenauigkeiten, was etwas nerven kann. Auch waren die Abstände bei sehr weiten Sprüngen für mich nicht immer ganz absehbar und ich stürzte ein paar Mail in die schier endlose Leere. Insgesamt funktioniert die Steuerung aber solide.

[h1]Schwierigkeit[/h1]
Der Schwierigkeitsgrad ist moderat. Rätsel können stellenweise fordernd sein, vor allem wenn man einen Mechanismus übersieht. An ein, zwei Stellen bin ich echt hängen geblieben und musste die Umgebung nochmal gründlich absuchen. Combat ist selten unfair, eher ruhig und kontrolliert.

[h1]Grafik[/h1]
Optisch ist „Hob“ ein echtes Highlight. Der Stil ist bunt, klar und trotzdem melancholisch. Die Welt wirkt lebendig, obwohl sie oft verlassen ist - ein spannender Kontrast. Besonders die Transformationen der Landschaft sehen richtig stark aus und sorgen für echte Wow-Momente. Auch die zu findenden Ausblicke ließen mich schon mal erstaunt zurück und machten Bock die Welt schnellstmöglich weiter zu erkunden.

[h1]Sound[/h1]
Der Soundtrack ist zurückhaltend, aber extrem stimmungsvoll. Viel Ambient, wenig aufdringlich - genau richtig für die Atmosphäre. Geräusche aus der Welt (Maschinen, Wind, Natur) tragen viel zur Immersion bei. Ich habe oft einfach kurz stehen geblieben und gelauscht.

[h1]Technik / Bugs[/h1]
Technisch lief das Spiel bei mir überwiegend stabil. Es gab vereinzelte kleinere Bugs, etwa mit der Kamera oder der Kollisionsabfrage. Ladezeiten sind kurz. Ich hatte leider auch einige Abstürze; sowohl kurz nach dem Laden eines Spielstandes als auch beim Wechsel der location (z. B. Eintritt in einen Dungeon). Außerdem hing ich an manchen Stellen fest, weil ich ungünstig gesprungen bin. Nichts super Spielzerstörendes, aber manchmal leicht irritierend und nervig.

[h1]Grind[/h1]
Sammelbares ist sinnvoll eingebettet und fühlt sich nicht nach Pflichtarbeit an. Wer alles upgraden will, muss natürlich erkunden und auch die currency grinden, aber das passt zum Spielgefühl. Verpflichtend ist nichts. Kein unnötiges Farming, kein künstliches Strecken. Ein Level-Up-System gibt es nicht. Man sammelt skills, die man im Hub kaufen muss; außerdem sammelt man Energie- und Gesundheitsupgrades.

[h1]Spielzeit / Umfang[/h1]
Für einen Durchgang sollte man bis zu 20 Stunden einplanen, je nachdem wie gründlich man erkundet. Completionist*innen sollten etwas mehr Zeit reinstecken. Das Tempo ist angenehm ruhig und lädt eher zum Entdecken als zum Durchrushen ein.

[h1]Errungenschaften / Achievements[/h1]
Viele Achievements ergeben sich automatisch durchs Spielen, andere erfordern gründliches Erkunden (z. B. Geschichtsräume finden, alle Schmetterlinge sammeln und alle Energie- und Gesundheits-Upgrades sammeln). Für 100 % ist es zwingend notwendig das game ein zweites Mal durchzuspielen, da sich die Sammel-Achievements mit dem Achievement „Schließe das Spiel ohne Schwert-, Gesundheits-, Energie- oder Laden-Upgrades ab“ ausschließen. Außerdem muss das game innerhalb von 5 Stunden durchgespielt werden und man muss das Spiel mit weniger als 5 Toden beenden - beide Errungenschaften gleichzeitig zu erhalten, ist vermutlich übelst schwer (zumindest für mich). Ich habe „Hob“ nicht auf 100 % gebracht. Ein Spieldurchlauf hat mir gereicht.

[h1]Preis[/h1]
Ich habe „Hob“ am 23.10.2024 für 3,99 € gekauft.

[h1]Fazit[/h1]
„Hob“ ist kein Spiel für Action-Junkies oder Story-Erklärbaren. Es lebt von Atmosphäre, Entdeckung und Stille. Wer Spiele wie „Journey“, „Rime“ oder „The Gunk“ mag, wird sich hier sehr wohlfühlen. Für mich ein leises, schönes Erlebnis mit Herz - unaufgeregt, aber nachhaltig 🌱✨.

[hr]Die Rezension spiegelt [u]meine ganz persönliche Meinung[/u] zu „Hob“ wider. Habt ihr inhaltliche, grammatikalische oder Rechtschreibfehler bemerkt oder habe ich etwas übersehen, bin ich euch für einen Hinweis dankbar.[/hr]

[h3][b]Some adventures speak best through the way the world opens in front of me[/b][/h3]

Hob is a wordless action adventure built around exploration, environmental puzzles, light combat, and a world that physically changes as I repair it. What stood out most to me was that constant sense of transformation, because unlocking new paths and seeing areas reconnect made exploration feel genuinely rewarding. I also liked its art direction and quiet atmosphere, which give the whole journey a calm but mysterious tone. It is not a combat heavy game, but that focus works in its favor. 

I enjoyed it because it trusted me to observe, experiment, and slowly understand how its world fit together. For me, that made even simple progression feel satisfying. My main warning is technical, because on Steam Deck I ran into serious performance drops that hurt the flow more than once. Even so, I still recommend it to players who enjoy exploration and puzzle driven adventures, but less to anyone expecting fast combat or a perfectly smooth handheld experience.

Comecei a jogar Hob hoje e já nas primeiras horas o jogo conseguiu me ganhar fácil. A gameplay é gostosa, o visual é lindo demais e dá para perceber que existe muito capricho em cada cenário. Tudo é muito bonito de olhar, cheio de detalhes, e a trilha sonora calma que fica tocando ao fundo deixa a experiência ainda mais imersiva. Em vários momentos eu simplesmente parei para apreciar o ambiente, porque o jogo realmente passa uma sensação muito boa de exploração e tranquilidade.
        
Uma das coisas que mais gostei foi justamente essa parte artística. Os cenários são variados, coloridos na medida certa e sempre despertam aquela vontade de ir mais longe para ver o que tem na próxima área. A trilha sonora acompanha muito bem isso, trazendo um clima relaxante que combina bastante com a proposta do jogo. A sensação de descoberta também é um ponto bem legal. Hob é aquele tipo de jogo que gosta de deixar você explorando por conta própria, encontrando caminhos escondidos e entendendo o mundo sem ficar te explicando tudo.

Mas nem tudo funciona tão bem assim. O que mais me incomodou foi a falta de direcionamento. Em muitos momentos eu fiquei andando sem saber exatamente para onde tinha que ir ou qual era o próximo objetivo. Tem hora que você não sabe se está esquecendo alguma coisa, se ainda falta habilidade ou se simplesmente passou batido pelo caminho certo. Isso acaba gerando uma frustração desnecessária.
Outro detalhe é que, por mais que a proposta seja exploração livre, o jogo poderia dar pelo menos um empurrãozinho em certos momentos. Um mapa mais claro ou algum indicativo visual já ajudaria bastante a não quebrar o ritmo. Além disso, em algumas partes de plataforma a movimentação parece um pouco imprecisa, e isso pode irritar quando o erro parece ser mais do jogo do que seu.

Minha conclusão é que no geral, Hob está sendo uma experiência muito agradável e bonita de acompanhar. É um jogo que encanta fácil pela atmosfera e pelo visual, mas também exige bastante paciência por deixar o jogador perdido com frequência. Mesmo assim, para quem gosta de explorar e descobrir tudo no próprio ritmo, vale bastante a pena.

O jogo é lindo, e muito legal, só queria que eles explorassem mais as mecânicas, como por exemplo a da corda que vc puxa,  os puzzles não eram nada demais e combate foi meio repetitivo. Gostei demais do jogo não possuir diálogos e a história ser bem escondida e aberta a interpretações. Recomendo esse jogo para quem quer relaxar e tirar a poeira do pc.

それでもジャンプで離れた足場に移る時、手前側から奥の方、またはその逆の方面にジャンプしようとすると、奥行のせいか踏み切り位置や飛ぶべき方向、着地可能な位置が分かり難く、横方向のジャンプ移動より落下する回数が多かったです。それもどうも3Dアクションでは昔から共通する難点のようなので、仕方ないのでしょう。

こうしたアクション作品に不慣れなせいか、最初は地面や壁にある黄色っぽい金属装飾が動線や目印だと気が付かず、迷子になっていました。
カメラ位置が固定ですが、ズプの素人でもそんなに不親切に感じた角度はたいしてないので、やり易い方なのだと思います。
思いのほか上下移動が激しく、高い所に登ったり飛び降りたり、下が完全に奈落な背景で狭い足場を歩いたり飛び移ったりしながら進む場面が多く、しかも3Dで表現されているので、高所が苦手な人は少し厳しいかもしれません。スティックでの細かい移動が難しくてよく落ちました。
良雰囲気ゲーではありますが、落下死したり大型の物に挟まれると血飛沫や赤いブロック塊になります。グロ苦手は人は注意です。

戦闘より、探索とギミックを動かして解くパズル要素が重要視されている内容です。
パズル要素もクリアするにはそんなに厳しくは感じませんでしたが、マップが広めで何かと移動が必要なので、人によっては一度手掛かりを見失うと迷う可能性が高いという主旨の指摘は正しいと思います。
全種類のアイテムや強化要素を取るためには、一部にかなり分かり難い動線を越えたり、隠し部屋を見つける必要があるようです。
[spoiler]進むにつれてマップの形が変わってゆくのは面白かったです。[/spoiler]

ガッツリ戦闘したい方にはぬる過ぎると思います。逆に言えば、探索の邪魔にならない程度の戦闘難易度に感じられます。
ローリング回避が無敵判定なのと、その辺の草刈りで回復用の玉がよく出るため、戦闘も何とかなりました。
一部のエリアに入ると強いザコ複数が出てきて、倒すとロックされていた場所が開く感じで、特定エンディングルート以外にラスボスはいません。
[spoiler]水中のあいつも倒したかったなあというのが残念なところです。何度喰われたことか。主人公血は赤いけど、大きいロボから手を移植できたから機械っぽいし美味くはないような。同じく水面に浮いている水鳥が喰われないのも理不尽感が増します。[/spoiler]
